stem: A straight support cable runs from a point on a vertical communications tower to an anchor in the level ground 16 meters from the base of the tower. The cable makes an angle of \(x^{\circ}\) with the ground, where \(\cos x^{\circ} = \frac{8}{17}\). How many meters above the ground is the cable attached to the tower?
solution: \(\cos x^{\circ} = \frac{16}{\text{cable}}\), so the cable is \(16 \div \frac{8}{17} = 34\) meters long.
verify:
c0=Rational(8,17)
Lc=16/c0
ans=sqrt(Lc**2-16**2)
assert Lc==34 and ans==30
assert all(Rational(s)==ans for s in spr_answers)
